cards.title: Four rings
cards.text: Device, campus, VSU-wide, and the internet. Each ring is meant to keep working when the rings outside it fail.

claims.text: What VSU makes would live on VSU's own network and servers first, with the internet as the outer ring, still open for everything from outside.
VSU has already built a fiber backbone, Wi-Fi across most of the Main Campus, and a typhoon-hardened data center on solar backup.
The campus intranet is a direction, not an ask.

cards.title: A question finds its answer
cards.text: In the network, a question would go to the office or person who can answer it. The confirmed answer would stay, dated and findable, and every notice would show who stands behind it.

claims.text: The network is built for three jobs: routing, memory, and trust.
In the network's design, questions are routed, not broadcast, and move to the office responsible when only an office can settle them.

cards.title: Wi-Fi access points
cards.text: In the campus-first design, access points would sit on each building's switches, sized for the people in a room, with sign-in by university account. Being on campus Wi-Fi alone would grant no trust.

claims.text: Access points would be sized by how many people use a space, with sign-in by university account.
Verified when accessed: every service checks who is asking, on campus or off.

cards.title: Switch and fiber
cards.text: In the campus-first design, the building's switch would join its access points to the fiber backbone, which runs to the data center at the campus core.

claims.text: VSU finished a new fiber backbone in 2017, after Typhoon Haiyan destroyed most of the old one in 2013.
Two fiber paths to each major building, so one cut does not isolate it.
The backbone's layout and redundancy are not public.

cards.title: Every post says what it is
cards.text: Official, community knowledge, opinion, unverified, scholarly, or external. In the network's design, only offices in official spaces post as official, and a notice shows whether it is current, updated, superseded, or archived.

claims.text: Every post carries one of six information types, and notices show whether they are current, updated, superseded, or archived.

cards.title: Kept for the next batch
cards.text: In the network's design, confirmed answers, guides, and notices stay, dated and findable. Discussion fades on a published schedule.

claims.text: The network keeps knowledge and lets conversation fade.
Because every kept answer makes the next question easier, the network's value compounds over the years.

cards.title: Saved on this phone
cards.text: The innermost ring would be the phone itself: it would keep the latest notices, so they open with no connection.

claims.text: A phone out of coverage still shows the notices it last synced.

cards.title: Scenes to come
cards.text: The problem scenes will sit here, at a kind of place. They are drawn next, and VSU evidence for them is still to come.

claims.text: A problem sits at a kind of place, never a named building or office, until VSU evidence ties it there.

cards.title: What a study will count
cards.text: A manual study would observe public VSU pages and groups by hand: where notices first appear and whether they change, and whether questions get answered, and by whom. Nothing is counted yet, and no group is named.

claims.text: The Facebook landscape study is manual and observation-only, and covers public VSU-related pages and groups.
No channel has been counted yet, and no day tallied.
The study names no community-run page or group.

cards.title: The scholarships place
cards.text: It would exist because scholarships do, and outlive every student who joins it. Its question boards could be split by kind: CHED, DOST-SEI, local government, private, and university scholarships.

claims.text: A place exists because what it serves exists, not because someone started a chat.
A large place can divide a board by topic, such as scholarships by kind.

cards.title: Boards inside a place
cards.text: Notices, questions, guides, events, and discussion. A place would open only the boards it needs, and what is superseded or past would go to its archive.

claims.text: Inside each place are boards for notices, questions, guides, events, and discussion.
A place opens only the boards it needs.

cards.title: Steward
cards.text: Looks after a place for a term: its boards, who may join, and the handover. An organization's officers would steward its place for their term, then pass it to the next officers.

claims.text: No one owns a place: stewards look after it for a term and hand it on, as an organization's officers would to the next officers.
The word steward is chosen over owner, and over admin, which is kept for running the platform.

cards.title: Moderator
cards.text: Keeps the place within the rules. A moderator would never remove a post for criticizing VSU, and never answer for an office: whether a post needs a response is the office's call.

claims.text: Moderators enforce the rules and never remove a post for criticizing VSU; offices answer concerns and never moderate.

cards.title: Peer guide
cards.text: A helper the place recognizes, shown on their posts, like a senior who keeps answering first-years. Helping would be recognized without public scores, levels, or rankings.

claims.text: The helper role in a place is called peer guide.
The network shows no public reputation scores, levels, or rankings.

cards.title: A VSU role is not a place role
cards.text: Faculty and staff would take part in their real roles, not as administrators. A faculty member who joins an organization's place is a member there; a student who stewards it has authority there and nowhere else.

claims.text: A member's role at VSU is separate from their role in a place, and no VSU role gives authority in a place by default.
Office accounts still post their offices' official notices.

cards.title: Roles still open
cards.text: Maintainers who keep guides current, contributors open to any volunteer: which other roles a place needs, what each may do, and for how long, is still open, to be designed with the prototype.

claims.text: Which roles a place has beyond steward, moderator, peer guide, and member, what each may do, and how and for how long each is given, is open.

scenes.title: One campus, two layers

heading.title: Project CAMPUS
heading.line: Connecting All Members, Places, and University Services
heading.note: A proposal for Visayas State University's Main Campus, by one alumnus. Nothing here is approved or built yet.

scenes.summary: The intranet on the ground: what VSU makes would live on VSU's own network first. The network above it: a question would reach someone who can answer, and the answer would stay.

claims.text: CAMPUS proposes a digital layer over the physical university, connecting its people, places, knowledge, and services.
One product, the social/academic network, with a campus intranet as its long-term infrastructure.

scenes.title: Inside an academic building
scenes.summary: Rooms and a hall. In the campus-first design, each has Wi-Fi access points on the building's switch, joined by fiber to the campus core.

claims.text: VSU finished a new fiber backbone in 2017, after Typhoon Haiyan destroyed most of the old one in 2013.
Access points on each building's switches, joined by fiber to the campus core.

scenes.title: A computer lab
scenes.summary: A whiteboard, tables and chairs, computers, and on one screen, the network: a department's community, open between tasks.

claims.text: The network is built first for the academic side of university life, with campus life around it.
Its communities are tied to real units, such as a department, each with a named owner.

scenes.title: The network, on a computer
scenes.summary: A department's community: an office notice labeled official and current, and a question with a confirmed answer, kept for the next batch.

claims.text: The first build is a small prototype of the network on made-up data.
Made-up content is marked as made up wherever it appears.

scenes.title: Between classes
scenes.summary: Outside the building, between classes, a student checks the same community on a phone.

claims.text: Outdoor access points where people gather, and wireless bridges where fiber cannot reach.

scenes.title: The same network, on a phone
scenes.summary: The same notice and the same kept answer, with the latest notices saved on the phone for when the signal drops.

claims.text: The first build is a small prototype of the network on made-up data.
A phone out of coverage still shows the notices it last synced.

scenes.title: One feed for everything
scenes.summary: A scholarship deadline, a lost ID, a dorm without water, a question about GIS: all in one feed. The feed doesn't know which office a post concerns, who it's for, or whether it's still true.

claims.text: Do students take institutional questions to unofficial groups, where peers answer and a wrong answer has no owner? Not yet known: the survey, the interviews, and the Facebook study will ask.
Do official notices and rumor look alike where campus talk happens? Not yet known: the survey and the Facebook study will ask.
A general platform knows nothing of VSU's roles, offices, or rules.

states.label: With CAMPUS
states.title: A place for every post
states.summary: On the network, each post would have a place, because what it's about exists at VSU: scholarships, a building, an organization, a dormitory. A place would outlive every student who joins it.

claims.text: In the network's design, every place is tied to something real at VSU: an office, a faculty or department, an organization, a council, a service, a subject, a residence, a building, a large yearly event, or an interest its members start.
Places sit side by side, never inside one another, and a place may say where it is.
Course sections are not places: their materials and grades stay in VSUEE.
Nothing about the network has been approved, built, or tested.

scenes.title: Stewards, not owners
scenes.summary: On the network, no one would own a place: stewards would look after it for a term, then hand it on. A faculty member who joins would be a member there, with no authority from their VSU role.

claims.text: In the network's design, no one owns a place: stewards look after it for a term, then hand it on.
A member's role at VSU is separate from their role in a place, and no VSU role gives authority in a place by default.
Which roles a place has beyond steward, moderator, peer guide, and member, such as maintainers of guides or contributors, is still open.
